slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
Chenin Blanc is the Loire Valley's 'king of white varieties' — the only grape in the world that can produce, from a single appellation, bone-dry mineral whites, delicate off-dry wines, honeyed botrytised treasures and fine sparkling wines. Understanding Chenin Blanc is the key to unlocking half of the Loire Valley.

Learning Objectives

⚡ Understand Chenin Blanc's defining character

Discover why sky-high natural acidity is the core of this variety's versatility

🏔️ Master dry Chenin — the mineral heights

Savennières, Vouvray sec — the world's greatest dry Chenin Blanc appellations

🍯 Explore sweet Chenin — liquid gold

From Coteaux du Layon to Quarts de Chaume Grand Cru — the full sweet-wine pyramid

⏳ Appreciate Chenin's ageing miracle

Great Chenin Blanc — dry or sweet — can age for 30 to 50+ years
slides.1.title: Chenin Blanc: The King of Varieties
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Extraordinarily High Natural Acidity
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Even at full ripeness, Chenin retains remarkable natural acidity — the secret to making balanced wines at every sweetness level
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The Most Versatile White Grape
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The same variety can produce mineral dry whites, floral off-dry wines, honeyed sweet wines and fine sparkling — all at the highest level
slides.1.content:
Among the world's great white varieties, Chenin Blanc is perhaps the most versatile. It is the anchor of the Loire Valley, appearing in styles ranging from bone dry to lusciously sweet, from still to sparkling.

🎭 The Chenin Blanc Style Spectrum

Sec (Dry)

Mineral, high acid, restrained fruit — best examples: Savennières, Vouvray sec

Demi-Sec (Off-Dry)

Balanced sweetness and acidity; floral and honeyed — best examples: Vouvray demi-sec, Montlouis

Moelleux / Liquoreux (Sweet)

Concentrated honey, apricot, quince; high residual sugar balanced by vibrant acidity — best examples: Quarts de Chaume, Bonnezeaux

Sparkling

Crémant de Loire and Saumur sparkling; Chenin's natural acidity makes the ideal base for bubbles

🗺️ Key Chenin Blanc Appellations

  • Savennières — dry, slate soils, mineral powerhouse
  • Vouvray / Montlouis — dry to sweet full spectrum, tuffeau soils
  • Coteaux du Layon — botrytised sweet wines, schist soils
  • Quarts de Chaume — Grand Cru, only 40 ha
  • Bonnezeaux — concentrated sweet, volcanic soils
slides.1.quiz.question: What is the most critical characteristic of Chenin Blanc that allows it to produce such a wide range of sweetness levels?
slides.1.quiz.options.0: Low acidity, making it easy to balance residual sugar
slides.1.quiz.options.1: Extremely high natural acidity, which keeps even high-sugar wines in balance
slides.1.quiz.options.3: Early ripening, allowing consistent harvests every year
slides.1.quiz.explanation: Chenin Blanc's exceptionally high natural acidity is the core reason it can span from bone dry to extremely sweet. High acidity balances residual sugar so that the wine never becomes cloying — instead displaying a fresh, lively sweetness. This is the secret behind why a Coteaux du Layon or Quarts de Chaume, despite extreme sweetness, remains utterly compelling.
slides.2.title: Dry Chenin — The Temple of Minerality
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Savennières: The Summit of Dry Chenin
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Savennières on Anjou's schist slopes is regarded as the pinnacle of dry Chenin Blanc; the celebrated Coulée de Serrant is an AOC within an AOC
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Vouvray: The All-Rounder
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Touraine's Vouvray can be dry, off-dry or sweet — and also sparkling — and excels at every level
slides.2.content:
At its driest, Chenin Blanc produces some of France's most extraordinary white wines — characterised by razor-sharp acidity, complex mineral layers and an ability to age for decades.

🏔️ Savennières

Location: Northern bank of the Loire, west of Angers

Soils: Dark schist and spilite

Style: Bone dry, austere in youth; develops extraordinary complexity with age — beeswax, quince, flint, ginger

Sub-appellations: Savennières-Roche-aux-Moines, Savennières-Coulée-de-Serrant (monopole, 7 ha, own AOC)

🏯 Vouvray sec

Location: East of Tours, tuffeau plateau

Soils: Tuffeau; underground cellars at constant temperature

Style: Dry to off-dry; green apple, pear, white flowers; gains beeswax and mineral complexity with age

Key producers: Domaine Huet, Domaine Foreau

🌊 Anjou Blanc / Saumur Blanc

Style: Crisp, mineral, straightforward expression of dry Chenin Blanc
slides.2.quiz.question: What is special about Savennières' most famous vineyard, Coulée de Serrant?
slides.2.quiz.options.0: It is the largest vineyard in the appellation
slides.2.quiz.options.1: It has its own independent AOC status and is famed for biodynamic farming
slides.2.quiz.explanation: Coulée de Serrant is not only just 7 hectares in size but also holds its own independent AOC status — a concept similar to a Burgundy Grand Cru with its own appellation. It is produced by Nicolas Joly's Château de la Roche aux Moines. Nicolas Joly is also a pioneering advocate of biodynamic viticulture (Biodynamie) in France.
slides.3.title: Sweet Chenin — Liquid Gold
slides.3.highlights.0.title: The Miracle of Botrytis
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Autumn mists bring Botrytis cinerea (noble rot), concentrating Chenin Blanc's sugars and creating enchanting sweet wines of honey, apricot and ginger
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Quarts de Chaume Grand Cru
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Just 40 hectares — the only sweet wine appellation in the Loire Valley to achieve independent 'Grand Cru' AOP status
slides.3.content:
In the right conditions — particularly the mist-laden autumns of Anjou — Chenin Blanc produces some of the world's most profound sweet wines, with an incomparable capacity for long ageing.

🍯 The Loire Sweet Wine Pyramid

🏆 Grand Cru Level

Quarts de Chaume Grand Cru — 40 ha, the only Loire sweet wine with independent Grand Cru AOP status (since 2011); schist and tuffeau soils; ages 50+ years

Bonnezeaux — schist and volcanic soils; deeply concentrated honey, quince and saffron

🥇 Premier Cru Level

Coteaux-du-Layon-premier-cru-Chaume — one step below Grand Cru

🍷 Appellation Level

Coteaux du Layon — the largest Loire sweet wine zone; botrytis and late harvest; wide range of styles and prices

Coteaux de l'Aubance — smaller, often overlooked; excellent value

🔬 The Sweet Wine Process

  • Harvested in multiple passes (tries successives) to select only botrytised grapes
  • Natural alcohol and residual sugar concentrated by Botrytis
  • Fermentation often halted naturally by high sugar levels
  • Aged in large old barrels or stainless steel to preserve freshness
slides.3.quiz.question: What is the unique status of Quarts de Chaume among Loire Valley sweet wines?
slides.3.quiz.options.0: It is the largest sweet wine appellation, hence the most prestigious
slides.3.quiz.options.1: It is the only Loire sweet wine appellation to achieve independent Grand Cru AOP status
slides.3.quiz.options.2: It only produces wine in even-numbered years
slides.3.quiz.options.3: Its Chenin Blanc is never made from botrytised grapes
slides.3.quiz.explanation: In 2011, Quarts de Chaume was awarded the Loire Valley's first (and to date only) Grand Cru independent AOP status, placing it on a par with a Burgundy Grand Cru in legal terms. Just 40 hectares in area, combined with strict low-yield rules, makes it a coveted rarity sought by collectors worldwide.
slides.4.title: Chenin Blanc's Ageing Miracle
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Time Is Chenin's Ally
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Top Chenin Blanc sweet wines can age for 50+ years, evolving from floral honey to complex layers of beeswax, apricot, ginger and mineral
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Dry Chenin's Astonishing Evolution
slides.4.highlights.1.content: A Savennières or top Vouvray sec after 15–20 years displays breathtaking complexity rivalling a Grand Cru white Burgundy
slides.4.content:
One of Chenin Blanc's most remarkable qualities is its extraordinary potential for long ageing. In great vintages and top appellations, both dry and sweet expressions develop complexity that few other white wines can match.

⏳ Chenin Blanc Aging Timeline

0–5 years: Youthful

Dry: green apple, pear, white flowers, fresh minerality | Sweet: honey, apricot, fresh acidity

5–15 years: Development

Dry: beeswax, quince, toast, deeper minerality | Sweet: caramelised peach, ginger, orange peel

15–30 years: Mature

Dry: petrol (petroleum), beeswax, mineral complexity, almost Grand Cru Burgundy-like | Sweet: saffron, honey, dried apricot, great aromatic complexity

30–50+ years: Peak

Rare, extraordinary expressions — Quarts de Chaume, Bonnezeaux, Coulée de Serrant at their finest

🍷 Serving Advice for Aged Chenin Blanc

  • Allow extra time to open in the glass — mature Chenin often needs air
  • Serve slightly cooler than Chardonnay (10–12°C for dry; 8–10°C for sweet)
  • Pair aged dry Chenin with foie gras, mature cheese or river fish
slides.4.quiz.question: After 20+ years of ageing, what aroma is a top Savennières (dry Chenin Blanc) most likely to develop?
slides.4.quiz.options.1: Petroleum, beeswax and complex mineral layers
slides.4.quiz.explanation: Aged fine dry Chenin Blanc — especially Savennières — is celebrated for developing a distinctive petroleum (kerosene) note, akin to aged Riesling, a hallmark of oxidative ageing in white wine. Intertwined with beeswax, quince, minerality and gingerbread, these complex aromas create an unrivalled multi-layered expression.
